title.narrative: AGROFORESTRY AND BIODIVERSITY FOR FOOD SECURITY AND RESILIENT LIVELIHOODS

description.narrative:
MVIWANYA is proposing a three-year project titled Agroforestry and Biodiversity for Food Security and Resilient Livelihoods, to be implemented in Tarime and Serengeti Districts from 2026 to 2028. The project is designed to address persistent challenges affecting smallholder farmers in these districts, including food insecurity, poverty, land degradation, and climate-related stress. Vulnerable groups particularly women, youth, children, and persons with disabilities face systemic barriers to land ownership, agricultural services, and economic participation.
The project will directly benefit 7,510 individuals from 1,876 households, focusing on restoring degraded land, improving agricultural productivity, and strengthening household and community resilience. Core targets include the rehabilitation of 5,000 hectares of land, planting of 450,000 agroforestry trees, and adoption of sustainable agricultural land management practices by at least 60% of participating households.
This initiative builds on MVIWANYA’s experience implementing the Agroforestry for Sustainable Livelihoods and Biodiversity (ASILI-B) programme, which demonstrated the effectiveness of community-led agroforestry and land restoration in selected areas. The current phase expands the approach to 30 wards and 110 villages that were previously not reached.
Implementation will follow a collaborative model involving local government authorities, technical institutions, civil society organizations, and private sector actors. Roles and responsibilities are clearly defined to ensure accountability, with oversight provided by MVIWANYA’s Board of Directors and Annual General Meeting, and operational leadership by the Project Coordinator and technical team.
The project is aligned with national development frameworks, including the Third Five-Year Development Plan (FYDP III), the Agricultural Sector Development Programme II (ASDP II), and the National Climate Change Response Strategy (NCCRS). It also contributes to the achievement of several Sustainable Development
Monitoring, evaluation, and learning will be guided by a structured PMERL framework, incorporating performance tracking tools, community feedback mechanisms, and safeguarding protocols. Evaluations will be conducted at baseline, annually, and at project completion to assess progress and inform adaptive management. Sustainability will be supported through community ownership, strengthened local institutions, and co-funding arrangements with Vi Agroforestry, alongside contributions from MVIWANYA. The project represents a practical and locally grounded effort to improve food security, restore ecosystems, and promote inclusive development in northern Tanzania.
